item.description: In January and February 2026, I had to spend a considerable amount of time in bed. To pass the time, I watched all the videos and read all the articles I could find about Italian synthesizers. I already understood that I had a strong fascination for analog poly-synths and, after some research, I began searching for a Crumar Bit 99.

item.description: Last month, I visited the Perret Tower in Grenoble, a concrete tower built in 1925. It is an amazing building that was closed for 60 years and recently restored. I took some pictures before and after the restoration and I built a music video featuring my music.

item.title: A new YouTube video: Chasing auroras.
item.description: I wrote a piece of music that predominantly features my Crumar Bit 99. It is atmospheric and dreamy, I hope you'll like it!

item.title: New link on the physics section of the website: cRCWA
item.description: The RCWA method is well known for solving Maxwell equations on periodic structures. cRCWA is an open source project that offers an efficient implementation of this method, plus some extension such as AFMM and the ability to take into account cylindrical coordinates.

item.title: New page on the website: Building a Turbokit replica for a GEM S2
item.description: I got a GEM S2 synthesizer in 1996. It was an early model, non Turbo. I used it for many years even on stage and it was a good instrument. I wanted to install a Turbokit back then, but I never got the occasion to do it. After 2005, I did not use the synthesizer very often until 2025 when I took it out again. A brief search revealed that DitroniX successfully managed to build a replica of GEM's original Turbokit and all the information I needed was available. I therefore installed a Gotek disk drive emulator in the synthesizer and proceeded to design and build my own Turbokit. This page describes the history of my synthesizer and how I managed to install the Gotek drive and (more importantly) the a replica of the Turbokit.

item.title: A new YouTube video: Impro on a Crumar BIT99 analog polysynth
item.description: I got recently a very nice Crumar BIT99 synthesizer. Similar to a certain extent to a Juno 106, it is a MIDI-controllable analog polysynth built in Italy from 1985 to 1987. I recorded a short improvisation with that nice synth, along with an Arturia Drumbrute Impact drum machine. Enjoy!

item.title: A new YouTube video: Liminal States
item.description: Hello! I wrote a new piece of music, called Liminal States and I recorded a YouTube video about it. It prominently features a fun electronic instrument from the 1970s, called a Stylophone. I hope you will enjoy.

item.title: A new page: Repairing my Commodore 64
item.description: Hi to all, I won a online auction for a broken C64 that wasn't working. It was the first time I tried to repair such a computer and I wanted to document in detail what I did on the machine. The post is therefore rather technical.

item.title: Updated the Revox B77 page: ball bearing or not?
item.description: Hi to all, I updated the page about the Revox B77 mk II. I study the effect of the popular mod that consists in replacing the original fixed roller on the right tape guide with a ball bearing. The results seem better with the original factory configuration, though.

item.title: Two new pieces of music
